questions.question: What is the most important client-side invariant for inline writing suggestions?
options: Typing must never wait for inference, and stale responses must be discarded.
Every eligible keystroke must produce visible text.
The largest available model must serve every request.
The client should retry until a suggestion appears.
questions.explanation: The feature is assistive. The compose surface remains authoritative and responsive even when inference is late or unavailable.

questions.question: A request spends 12 ms on the network, 8 ms on context, 6 ms waiting for a batch, 27 ms on inference, and 5 ms on release checks. Does it fit a 60 ms budget?
options: Yes, with 2 ms of headroom.
Yes, with 12 ms of headroom.
No, it exceeds the budget by 2 ms.
It cannot be determined without model accuracy.
questions.explanation: The complete path is 58 ms. Budget every stage because a fast model cannot compensate for unbounded network or queue time.

questions.question: Why can a 95% confidence candidate still be suppressed?
options: Confidence replaces only the latency check.
It may be stale, unsafe, in the wrong language, or no longer match the active prefix.
High confidence means the candidate is too predictable.
The system should show only low-confidence candidates.
questions.explanation: Confidence is one release condition. Freshness, current-prefix identity, policy, and language are independent gates.

questions.question: Which work should stay off the synchronous keystroke path?
options: Prefix identity validation
Candidate policy filtering
Model training and aggregate analytics
The final client freshness check
questions.explanation: Training and analytics are asynchronous. Only the minimum work required to produce and release a safe, current suggestion belongs on the request path.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the suggestion service misses its deadline?
options: Block the editor until a retry succeeds.
Render the late suggestion after the user stops typing.
Return no suggestion and let typing continue normally.
Reuse another user's cached completion.
questions.explanation: No suggestion is a valid degraded state. The assistive feature must not interrupt the primary compose workflow.

questions.question: Why should personalization be separated from the global candidate model?
options: So account-scoped style signals can be controlled, audited, and disabled without changing the shared model contract.
So personalized suggestions can be shared across tenants.
So the client can bypass safety filters.
So raw message content can be retained indefinitely.
questions.explanation: A separate account-scoped layer creates a clearer privacy and control boundary while preserving a generic fallback.

questions.question: Which metric pair best reveals whether a low-latency rollout actually helps users?
options: Average GPU utilization and model parameter count only
Suggestion coverage and accepted characters, sliced alongside dismissals and policy suppressions
Training loss and repository size only
Request count and cache size only
questions.explanation: Latency is necessary but not sufficient. Product value and harm require behavioral, quality, and safety metrics segmented by language and cohort.
